title: Token Cost Scenario Grid & Export — Pricing Patterns for Console
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design a compact, scannable Token Cost Scenario Grid component for the Redwood Console that lets users build, compare, and export pricing scenarios at token granularity. Deliverables: high-fidelity grid prototype, CSV/JSON export flow, copy/specs for pricing pattern variants (per-token tiering, bundling, per-route overrides), accessibility review, and handoff artifacts for engineering. \n\nWhy: Customers need an easy way to simulate cost impact of batching, quantization, and routing policies across multiple routes/models, then export those scenarios for finance and procurement. This feature complements the cost-attribution panels and targets platform teams and PMs evaluating Dedicated commitments.
acceptance_criteria: Grid supports up to 20 scenario rows and 8 columns (model, avg tokens, batch policy, quantization profile, route, estimated cost, latency impact, notes)
Export produces CSV with raw numeric fields and JSON with metadata (labels, creation date, linked routes)
Prototype annotated with interaction states and edge cases (empty state, partial data, conflicting policies)
Design tokens and spacing match Console system; components accessible (keyboard nav, screen reader labels)
Engineering sign-off on feasibility for initial iteration within runtime-1.20 roadmap
design_notes: Chose grid over card list to enable rapid side-by-side comparisons and CSV-shaped export
Trade-off: grid density vs. readability. Default row height increased + line clamp on notes to preserve scanability
Decision: show estimated cost as both per-request and per-month estimate (configurable toggle) to help finance conversations
We delay per-token drilldown heatmaps to v2 to keep MVP small and ship export first
